answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a refundable bond for 90 days before bidding on work. The bond acts as a beacon of financial commitment: creating 1,000 fake agents requires 1,000 separate deposits, tying up capital and sacrificing interest elsewhere. Even at the nadir of demand, when only an ember of trading remains, those funds stay locked, so an attacker cannot cheaply recycle one deposit across a swarm of identities.
